'''Karl Anker Jørgensen''' (born 15 June 1955) is a Danish chemist whose research has focused on [[organic chemistry]], particularly [[organocatalysis]], [[asymmetric synthesis]] and stereoselective reaction design.<ref>{{cite web |title=Scientific contributions of Karl Anker Jørgensen |url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Karl-Anker-Jorgensen-2163101386 |website=ResearchGate |access-date=18 November 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.au.dk/en/kaj@chem.au.dk/ |title=Karl Anker Jørgensen |website=[[Aarhus University]] |access-date=8 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.groupjorgensen.com/ |title=Jørgensen Group |website=Group Jørgensen |access-date=8 April 2026}}</ref> He has been associated with the [[Department of Chemistry]] at [[Aarhus University]] where he has worked on [[catalytic]] methods for the preparation of [[chiral molecules]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.au.dk/en/kaj@chem.au.dk/ |title=Karl Anker Jørgensen |website=[[Aarhus University]] |access-date=8 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Marigo |first1=M. |last2=Francinelli |first2=M. |last3=Bencivenni |first3=G. |last4=Fini |first4=C. |last5=Schmidtchen |first5=F.P. |last6=Jørgensen |first6=K. A. |title=Enantioselective Organocatalyzed α-Sulfenylation of Aldehydes |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |volume=51 |issue=31 |pages=7546–7550 |year=2012 |doi=10.1002/anie.201201019 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/anie.201201019/pdf|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
